name: New Mexico

response.rule_text: Custodian must permit inspection not later than 15 days after a written request; if not within 3 business days it must explain in writing when records will be available (§ 14-2-8(D)). Unit of the 15 days is not labeled by RCFP (calendar inferred).

fees.labor_rule: No fee for the cost of determining whether a record is subject to disclosure (§ 14-2-9(C)(6)); commonly read to bar search fees.
fees.copy_rule: Reasonable copy fee, not over $1 per page up to 11x17; download at actual cost plus device cost (§ 14-2-9(C)).
fees.late_penalty: Court awards damages, costs and attorney fees to prevailing requester (§ 14-2-12(D)).

residency.rule_text: Every person has the right to inspect public records (§ 14-2-1).

appeal.body: State District Court (Attorney General or district attorney may also enforce)
appeal.rule_text: No administrative appeal or ombudsman; sue in district court or ask AG/DA to enforce (§ 14-2-12). RCFP gives no firm deadline (suit likely not barred for at least two years).

format_rule: Electronic copy provided if available electronically, in the format existing at request time (§ 14-2-9(B)); no duty to create records (§ 14-2-8(B)).
notes: Two halves read. Denial may be deemed after 15 days (§ 14-2-10); excessively burdensome requests get extension with written notice within 15 days. Governor has qualified executive privilege. Legislature covered but disputes legislator emails (Joint Rule 12-1). RCFP chapter last updated Aug 2021. Response days null: the 15-day unit is not labeled by RCFP; rule stays in rule_text.
